byte_extents.fact: Table index is u16(event_index * 12 + phase), entries are 12 bytes; operation runs before next phase is written.
All 21 opcodes 0x3400 through 0x3414 have the event order exposed by Queue36Event; other opcodes return zero.
The 21 by 12 table contains only no-operation and operation-with-next-phase cells; no completion-function cells occur.
Event 12 (0x340a) state 4 is operation 0x00d84ff8 with next phase 6: it calls +0x404 slot 0xc like event 9 state 4 (0x00d84d70, next phase 5). Event 4 (0x3406) state 4 is 0x00d84384, status -14.

For +0x3f0 == 2 the calls are +0x404 slot 4, +0x408 slot 0 (0x00d954c0, clears 0x0146af98 and 0x0146af9b), +0x408 slot 4 (0x00d953cc, initializes when 0x0146af98 is zero), timer 250, +0x404 slot 0x1c with 0x00d82178, timer 60000. For 3 it calls +0x3fc slot 8 with +0x3f4 and +0x3f8.

In phases 8 to 11 the dispatcher calls 0x00d7b830 first, for kinds 6 and 10 only when the first payload word is nonzero. Kinds 4 and 5 call +0x3fc slots 0xc and 0x10; kinds 6, 7, 8, 10, 9, 12, 13, 14, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21 call +0x42c, +0x430, +0x434, +0x43c, +0x438, +0x440, +0x444, +0x448, +0x450, +0x454, +0x458, +0x45c, +0x464, +0x468; every other kind returns.

Completion registration stores handle 0 when d7b98c is not 1, otherwise 21 when d7b9ac is zero or 23 when nonzero. It stores callback at +0x414, posts 0x3402, and invokes the installed callback immediately only in the connected branch.
Open registration stores r1 at +0x3f0, r0 at +0x418, r2 at +0x3f4 and r3 at +0x3f8 before posting 0x3403.
Primary polling registers period 25 for argument zero or 500 for argument one, periodic mode 1, callback d813ac and output handle +0x3cc through actual69b328.
Primary cancellation uses actual69b7a4, then clears +0x3cc and +0x3c4.

Long/short callbacks post 0x3411/0x3410. Secondary/primary callbacks coalesce using +0x3c8/+0x3c4; primary also calls the task-priority wrapper 0x00723a14 with (36, 8) at 0x00d81410..0x00d81418 after posting 0x340d.
The poll tail calls the task-priority wrapper 0x00723a14 with (36, 11) at 0x00d81e1c..0x00d81e24 unless the handle changed to connected.
Deferred messages use 20 slots, preincrement modulo20 indices and a blocked flag; the task drains deferred messages before blocking on queue36.
Protocol mode2 starts the periodic50 secondary registration after clearing connection-active and pending fields.
Short transfer timer is period250, periodic mode1.
Long transfer timer is period60000, periodic mode1.
Actual installed consumers publish queue7 b400(status), b401(empty), 1714(handle,status), b403(handle,status), b404(status). Closed is the only b401 producer among these consumers.

ownership.controller_runtime.rs: Queue36 ABI, event/phase selection, deferred scheduler, registration writers, status publication and retained Service completion bridge.
ownership.controller_registration.rs: Owned timer callbacks and timer handle lifetime using canonical Power registry start/release.
ownership.controller.rs: Retained event6 shutdown and command-completion controller.
ownership.transport.rs: Retained actual DMA and teardown CPU.
ownership.service.rs: Retained actual wire session and command CPU.
ownership.provider_composition: VendorProtocolJoin integrates concrete UsbStart, connection, PTP and DPS providers into the complete action driver. An operation selector alone is not completed CPU.

integration_contract.construction: The root owns the RTOS engine. On ARM ControllerRoot::new takes the producers from controller_root::native::TIMER_PRODUCERS, the instance the four timer entries fire; a host root takes the instance passed to new. ControllerRuntime::new(service, &producers) lifetime-borrows that producer state. Its timer handles are the canonical Rust-owned registration slots, not copies of legacy native slots.
integration_contract.shutdown: Put the single RTOS engine in RefCell. Call registrations.shutdown_parts(&mut connection, &mut deferred, &rtos). Pass parts.storage, parts.short and parts.long to ShutdownResources with SharedRtos(&rtos). The adapter synchronously posts actual171a before canonical secondary release and clears the same ConnectionState activity.
integration_contract.native_timers: NativeTimerRegistry borrows canonical NativeRegistrationRegistry and root-owned TimerCallbackEntries. Each noarg entry must resolve the root's stable admitted context or typed callback registry, then call the same TimerProducers::fire(TimerEvent, rtos). The ARM root's producers are the static controller_root::native::TIMER_PRODUCERS instance the entries fire.
integration_contract.unclosed_native_prerequisite: The final root must install lifetime-safe noarg callback context binding before constructing NativeTimerRegistry. Supplying function addresses alone does not complete this join.
integration_contract.driver: The final root executes every ControllerOperation against actual UsbStart, connection, Service, PTP and DPS CPU before applying table_next_state. Dynamic phase writes remain operation-owned. Deferred messages must be selected before native queue receive; shutdown messages are never consumed by Service.
dependencies: Power e366600b plus Services 376acba3 canonical timer API
VendorProtocolJoin Service consume_queue_completion and QueueController handle accessors
forbidden_shortcuts: No callback dispatch trait replaces the action driver
No arbitrary guest function pointer execution
No native-only or host-only completion claim

qualification.scope: Source implementation and behavioral source tests only; no execution or whole-unit completion claim.
